heard: Billions of planets drift through total darkness without any star at all. Most people assume every single planet belongs to a solar system, bound tightly to a shining sun. Instead, massive nomadic objects known as rogue planets wander the vast galaxy in absolute solitude. Astronomers first identified a massive population of these mysterious objects back in 2011 using gravitational microlensing techniques. That clever observational technique reveals invisible worlds when their gravity warps the light of distant background stars. Recent research suggests these lonely wanderers significantly outnumber starbound worlds by six to one. Trillions of invisible worlds continue drifting through total darkness without any star at all.
